items.title: Square Enix Announces Final Fantasy XIV's First-Ever Eorzean Symphony World Tour for 2027
items.summary: Square Enix has announced the first-ever world tour of its acclaimed Final Fantasy XIV orchestral concert, giving fans across North America, Europe and Asia the opportunity to experience music from the game performed live.
items.content:
News Square Enix Announces Final Fantasy XIV’s First-Ever Eorzean Symphony World Tour for 2027 Image by Charlotte Davis Add Essential Japan on Google Follow Essential Japan on Google Discover Add Essential Japan on Google Follow Add Square Enix has announced the first-ever world tour of its acclaimed Final Fantasy XIV orchestral concert, giving fans across North America, Europe, and Asia the opportunity to experience music from the game performed live.

The “FINAL FANTASY XIV ORCHESTRA CONCERT 2027 -Eorzean Symphony-” will feature 13 performances across ten cities, bringing together a full orchestra, choir and two of the game’s original vocalists.

The Eorzean Symphony concert series first debuted in Japan in 2017, presenting specially arranged orchestral versions of music from the hugely popular massively multiplayer online role-playing game.

Four sold-out Japanese concert series have taken place in 2017, 2019, 2022 and 2025, alongside several standalone overseas performances, with the upcoming tour marking the first time the concert has embarked on a coordinated international tour of this scale.

Music has played an important role in the success of Final Fantasy XIV, with composer Masayoshi Soken and the game’s wider sound team creating an extensive soundtrack that accompanies players throughout their adventures across Eorzea and the other worlds introduced through successive expansions.

The upcoming concerts will be conducted by Hirofumi Kurita, who will be joined by returning guest vocalists Amanda Achen and Jason Charles Miller.

Both singers have contributed to some of the game’s most memorable musical moments, with Achen performing songs such as “Tomorrow and Tomorrow” and “Flow,” while Miller provided vocals for “Shadowbringers” and “To the Edge”.

Although the complete setlist for the world tour has yet to be revealed, the performances will revisit music associated with the emotional storylines, dramatic battles, and adventures experienced by players throughout the game.

Square Enix has also continued expanding its catalog of orchestral recordings, having released the fourth Eorzean Symphony orchestral album earlier this year.

The Blu-ray album includes orchestral arrangements of music from A Realm Reborn, Heavensward, Stormblood, Shadowbringers, Endwalker and Dawntrail, alongside concert footage recorded during the December 2025 performances at the Tokyo International Forum.

Fans of the game’s music have also received a new collection of solo piano arrangements through the recently released FINAL FANTASY XIV Piano Collections – Till Dawn My Tears Flow album , which includes a bonus recording of “Bee My Honey” performed at the 2026 Fan Festival in Anaheim.

The world tour will arrive shortly after the release of the game’s next major expansion, Final Fantasy XIV: Evercold, which is scheduled to launch in February 2027 and is receiving its own official Collector’s Goods Box featuring an elaborate Reaper statue .

Produced by Square Enix in collaboration with PROMAX and SOHO Live, the Eorzean Symphony world tour will begin in Thailand before traveling through Europe and Asia, concluding with four performances across Canada and the United States.

items.title: More FFXIV Cross-Region Data Center Travel Options Announced
items.summary: Square Enix will bring back cross-region data center travel head of FFXIV Evercold for a limited time and with new options.
items.content:
Square Enix announced it will try to mitigate Final Fantasy XIV server congestion ahead of FFXIV Evercold with cross-region data center travel for the European, Japanese, and North American ones. There will be limitations as to where subscribers’ Warriors of Light can go, however. It also isn’t available now, and will instead start on December 1, 2026.

We first heard about the cross-region data center travel opportunities way back in March 2024 when Square Enix announced a test ahead of FFXIV Dawntrail that allowed people on the European, Japanese, and North American ones to head to Oceania . That was implemented to assist with congestion ahead of that expansion’s release. Once that happened, Square Enix noted there were requests for that sort of travel between the European and North American ones.

So when December 2026 starts, anyone on the European, Japanese, and North American can head to Oceanian data centers. However, people in Europe will be able to head to the North American ones too, and people in North America could choose to go to Europe as well. This will be temporary again for now, but the company also acknowledged the demand for it to possibly become permanent and mentioned considering it .

This is one of two major data center-related changes to show up at the end of 2026. Same-region player matching is available in the MMORPG now. That happened in Japan in 7.57, then in Europe and North America in 7.58 .

Fi nal Fantasy XIV is available for the Switch 2, PS4, PS5, Xbox Series X, and PC, and cross-region data center travel will appear between North America and Europe on December 1, 2026. FFXIV Evercold will debut on February 23, 2027 . There will be an early access phase for that expansion that will begin on February 19, 2027 for those who qualify due to certain edition purchases.

items.title: Final Fantasy 14 Is Letting Players Travel Between North American And European Servers For The First Time In 16 Years And Fans Are Psyched
items.summary: Mr. Yoshida, tear down this wall
items.content:
Whenever there’s a new Final Fantasy XIV expansion, especially one as hotly anticipated as Evercold is, queues to log into the game infamously become a slog. To combat this inevitable server congestion, Square Enix has announced that it will permit cross-region travel between North American and European data centers.

Starting after the scheduled maintenance on December 1st, players will be able to hop between North American and European data centers at will, or pop over to the Oceanian data centers if they so choose. Here’s the breakdown of the new server traffic flows:

Cross-region Travel Available Beginning Tuesday, December 1, 2026

To help alleviate server congestion following the release of Patch 8.0, we will be enabling cross-region Data Center Travel between the North American and European data centers during scheduled maintenance on Tuesday, December 1, 2026.

— FINAL FANTASY XIV (@en.finalfantasyxiv.com) 2026-11-24T12:00:45.707Z

Square Enix’s reasoning is quite simple; peak player times vary across regions so when the servers are slammed in North America, players can choose a European data center to potentially sidestep thousand-player-deep log-in queues and vice versa. ot only is this a great way to get ahead of the impending server traffic jam, but it’s also a neat social feature that eases some of the siloing that happens between servers.

Currently, if you have a cross-continental friendship, you’d have to make an alternate character on the appropriate data center in order to play together. Cross-region travel will let you port your main character over, letting you quest together and, critically, run endgame content like raids without the need to start from scratch on a new server. That’s huge and players are suitably hyped for it, hoping that the option to data-center-hop remains available permanently.

Square Enix warns that visiting other data centers might increase latency and encourages players to test it out before Evercold launches in February 2027 to get a feel for it. Also, sorry to Oceanian data center players, you still don’t get to go anywhere for now.

items.title: "Encouraging players to return is no mean feat" - Square Enix tempts Final Fantasy 14 players back with free game-time to fill void before new expansion
items.summary: FF14 producer Naoki Yoshida says retaining active players is of "utmost importance", as Square Enix tempts players back with free game time.
items.content:
"People pause their adventures for all kinds of reasons."

Image credit: Square Enix News by Connor Makar Reporter Published on Nov. 17, 2026, 11:48 a.m. 3 comments Follow Final Fantasy XIV: Evercold Prioritise us on Google Final Fantasy 14 is between expansions at the moment, with Evercold preparing for release in February. So, in order to keep the game populated for the next few months, Square Enix is running a special promotion in hopes of tempting players back in.

This promotion, which began yesterday, offers players a choice between two enticing freebies. Lapsed players who haven't logged in for over six months are to be given 30 days of free game time to hop back in and catch up with the main story quest ahead of Evercold's release.

In addition, there's an alluring character skip available too. If your FF14 character is at least level 90 on one class - the current level-cap is 100 - you can skip all the way to the final part of the latest Dawntrail expansion. You still need to grind to level 100 in preparation for Evercold, but the aforementioned free month of game time should provide plenty of time to do so.

In a producer letter written to accompany this promotion , Naoki Yoshida provided insight into why this was being implemented, stating that retaining players in an MMO like FF14 was of the "utmost importance".

"Encouraging players to return is no mean feat", Yoshida wrote. "People pause their adventures for all kinds of reasons, including dissatisfaction and loss of interest. Although we continually update the game to address such issues, the fact remains that getting players to resume their journey is a difficult task indeed.

"For one, I feel that the pace of change in our lives is growing increasingly fast. Back when A Realm Reborn launched, I set policies in place based on the idea that significant changes in life usually happened in roughly three-year cycles. With that in mind, we've done our best to avoid heavy-handed attempts to secure player retention through game design, and we still maintain that philosophy even today."

Yoshida went on to explain that promotions such as this are meant as a "tiny nudge". He notes that those who have retained subscriptions continuously remain "the most important" players in the development team's eyes, and acknowledges that the process of catching up in an MMO can seem "daunting" for many.

This problem of player retention is nothing new for MMOs, especially in the tricky time between the end of a current expansion and the beginning of a new one. MMO popularity often waxes and wanes, with a new expansion acting as an exciting call to action, with the months leading up to it often serving as a natural break-point for many. Still, monthly subs pay the bills, so keeping folks around even during these quiet months is important.

Final Fantasy 14: Evercold is looking like an especially exciting expansion. On top of the new story and two classes being added, the game is getting an overhaul to combat, with both classic Reborn and Evolved action modes, as well as a new raid difficulty meant to bridge the gap between normal and savage tiers.

The game has certainly come a long way since its initial release back in 2010. Dawntrail proved divisive among fans too , though with Evercold there's a lot of hope that a new overarching storyline can bring the steal back the hearts of players old and new.

items.title: FF14 Free Trial Extended To Lapsed Players Ahead Of Evercold
items.summary: In preparation for Evercold, Square Enix is giving away 30 days of free game time to eligible players and has a new item for purchase that'll let you skip Dawntrail
items.content:
If you are like me and haven’t played Final Fantasy XIV in a minute, now might be the time to jump back in and finally get through Dawntrail before the new expansion launches in 2027. Starting November 16, players who haven’t logged in to the paid MMORPG in the last five months (150 days specifically) are eligible for 30 days of free playtime.

Players have from November 16th to January 14, 2027 to claim their free 30 days, which means that, if you time it right, your free period will overlap with the launch of the $45 Evercold expansion on February 23. Square Enix has all the specifics here .

The Road to Evercold begins today, helping you prepare for the upcoming release of Evercold!

⭐ 30-day Free Login Campaign ⭐ Tales of Adventure: Winter's Prelude

— FINAL FANTASY XIV (@en.finalfantasyxiv.com) 2026-11-16T10:30:05.686Z

Digging into the details, it seems like Square Enix knows a lot of people (including me) lit out after Endwalker and haven’t been back to play the latest expansion, Dawntrail. In addition to offering free game time, Square Enix is also offering a new $10 Tales of Adventure item which lets players auto-skip main story quest content. It’s designed specifically to leap-frog players over Dawntrail stuff, taking them from the end of Endwalker to the beginning of “In Fate’s Footsteps,” this year’s Evercold -introducing 7.5 event patch.

It is powerfully seductive to pay $10 bucks to take the coward’s way out of Dawntrail . I’ve heard that expansion is just okay, and possibly even worth skipping. But I play Final Fantasy XIV for its story. It can’t always be Heavensward or Shadowbringers , sometimes there has to be a Stormblood in there and that’s okay. As I try to take advantage of the free game time, I’ll finally see Dawntrail for myself.

items.title: How a data centre united Australia's gaming community
items.source: ABC News & Headlines – Australian Broadcasting Corporation
items.summary: After years of playing on distant worlds, Australian gamers of the popular Japanese role-playing game Final Fantasy XIV discovered a new home. Now that community has welcomed the game developers Down Under.
items.content:
Michael-Christopher Koji Fox (left) and Toshio Murouchi (right) were the main attractions for players at PAX Australia. ( Supplied: Square Enix )

Link copied Share Share article Before the Oceania data centre arrived, Australians sometimes found the online role-playing game Final Fantasy XIV a surprisingly lonely multiplayer experience.

On the Asia server, they'd struggle to find enough fellow English speakers to tackle the game's notorious super-bosses. Those visiting American servers would find the in-game Golden Saucer amusement park sparsely populated during another time zone's twilight hours.

And the few who chose the most distant Europe server struggled with "input lag" that perilously delayed gameplay actions, with the risk of failed quests and let-down teammates.

That changed in January 2022, 12 years after the game was released, when, encouraged by a pandemic boom in player numbers, developer Square Enix finally launched Oceania servers. It was a decision that united players in the region.

Lin, a Final Fantasy XIV community organiser from Melbourne, was shocked at the scale of the local player base.

"When they finally released a server where our ping [internet connection latency speed] was manageable, we were like, 'whoa, there's thousands of people here'," they tell ABC Arts.

"It took 30 minutes just to get into the queue. You no longer had to guess if we could speak the same language or understand the same lingo."

Final Fantasy's near-40-year legacy lured Pat, another community organiser from Melbourne, into online role-playing games.

"I love the Final Fantasy series. That's the one I grew up with," they say.

The Final Fantasy series has nabbed more than 212 million sales. ( Supplied: Square Enix )

By nature, Final Fantasy XIV's community primarily exists online. A community organisation called Jjammin' runs in-game award shows, theatre shows and musical productions throughout the year.

For many in the region's broader Final Fantasy XIV community, the annual Limsa Extreme meet-up at PAX Australia, one of the country's biggest exhibitions of games and gaming culture, is the highlight on the calendar.

Limsa Extreme was created in 2022 by head organiser Kiya, who was determined to make up for the absence of official events and meetups in Australia. Since then, the event has drawn players from across ANZ, Malaysia and Indonesia, and now even the Japan-based developers.

items.title: Final Fantasy 14, Umamusume: Pretty Derby, and more impacted as PHP vulnerability outages hit games around the globe
items.summary: If left unaddressed, the PHP vulnerability may have resulted in serious security issues for games including Final Fantasy 14 and Umamusume: Pretty Derby.
items.content:
Image credit: Eurogamer / Square Enix News by Connor Makar Reporter Published on Oct. 22, 2026, 2:11 p.m. 24 comments Follow Final Fantasy XIV: Shadowbringers Prioritise us on Google Multiple games - including Final Fantasy 14 and Umamusume: Pretty Derby - have faced outages and other issues following this week's discovery of a serious PHP vulnerability.

This vulnerability could potentially result in substantial security breaches for the massive number of websites and applications built using the PHP programming language. As a result, it was advised that online services built upon it should be taken offline until a fix could be distributed and applied. Inevitably, games were caught up.

An official post made to the Final Fantasy 14 lodestone website informed users that security "enhancements" were being made to the MMO's patch servers. As a result, new logins were temporarily disabled until the updates could be completed. While logins have since been turned back on , the server back-up feature for user's save data remains offline.

Horse racing gacha game Umamusume: Pretty Derby, meanwhile, was taken offline completely . As its server-side infrastructure uses PHP, a sudden maintenance outage was put in place - though its developer assured players no exploitation of the security vulnerability had occurred. Right now, Japanese and global servers are back online, with a compensatory package of in-game currency being sent to all players.

Path of Titans, an in-beta dinosaur MMO (which sounds awesome by the way) is still down as of writing. In an announcement made to its official X account , developer Alderon Games explained the MMOand its website had been taken down for up to three days as a precautionary measure. Players were also assured no data had been compromised.

One hopes the chaos is largely over now a fix is in circulation. But even if it is, the fact that so many services all across the globe - far beyond the games industry - have rushed to protect the sanctity of their data and that of their users speaks to the seriousness of the situation. Take a moment to thank the tech heads out there who may have had to work around the clock to get this sorted.

items.title: The Final Fantasy 14 Typing Minigame Isn't Even Out Yet And It's Already Pissing Players Off
items.summary: Hardware requirements and gender-locked rewards aren't getting players excited
items.content:
Final Fantasy VII Rebirth Final Fantasy XIV Square Enix

Earlier this year, Final Fantasy XIV announced that it would feature several crossover events with Square Enix’s other golden goose IP, the Final Fantasy VII remake project. In addition to featuring a raid series themed around the remake trilogy, the MMO would also add a new minigame to Gold Saucer which, like its FF7 counterpart, is a place where Eorzeans can gamble gil and partake in other leisurely, less world-savey pursuits. But though the minigame, called Keybound Brawler, isn’t out yet, it’s already pissing people off.

Keybound Brawler will be landing in the Manderville Gold Saucer on October 28, and the first iteration of the event will be a special collaboration with the FINAL FANTASY VII REMAKE series! ⌨️ https://t.co/5yNsdKqbV1 pic.twitter.com/JR3Yujh8Hr

— FINAL FANTASY XIV (@FF_XIV_EN) October 21, 2026

Keybound Brawler is a typing game ala Typing Of The Dead which requires the use of a keyboard to complete. However, FFXIV has a rather large console player base and it seems like there’s quite a few of them who don’t keep a keyboard in arm’s reach. It’s a simple, relatively cheap fix, sure, but it’s the principle, you see. On social media and the game’s subreddit, console players are upset at having to buy or otherwise procure a keyboard to experience part of a game they’ve been playing just fine with a simple controller for over a decade—especially since the game just launched on the Switch 2, opening up a whole new avenue of console players.

But Keybound Brawler’s worst offense is in its gender-locked rewards. In the first iteration of the minigame, players can win costumes that can dress up Warriors of Light as either Barret or Tifa, but only male characters can wear Barret’s clothes and females only Tifa’s. Naturally, in the community for which “glamour is the endgame,” this ain’t going over well.

deeply disappointing that the gear is genderlocked. what about that promise to stop genderlocking cosmetics. i was going to resub for this event but i just cant be bothered if y'all still cant keep your word

— twink death ☁️💫 (@catboyfriencl) October 21, 2026

The curious restriction flies in the face of previous moves Square Enix has made with clothing and gender. Way back in 2020, game director Naoki Yoshida announced that the gender restriction on the game’s wedding outfits would be removed . Before the Endwalker expansion, Square Enix did it again, removing the gender restriction on maid outfits which is the morally correct thing to do right before making male Viera a character option. It’s odd, then, to see Square Enix go back to such restrictions for something that would generate as much player interest as this.

Please unlock the glams for both genders, I want to dress my Clive Rosfield alt in the Tifa glam just like Ben Starr XD

— The_One_True_Clive_Rosfield (@CliveRosfield44) October 21, 2026
